findings: Source is BT Group plc Annual Report 2025 (Companies House consolidated group accounts, filed 2025-08-08); FY25 = year ended 31 March 2025; Strategic report approved/signed 22 May 2025 (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/BT-A.L/20260904T201714Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_04190816_MzQ3NjUzNTMzOWFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Contents-page 'How we've done' KPIs (FY25 vs FY24): revenue £20.4bn (−2% vs FY24 £20.8bn); profit before tax £1.3bn (+12% vs £1.2bn); adjusted EBITDA £8.2bn (+1% vs £8.1bn); cash flow from operating activities £7.0bn (+17% vs £6.0bn); normalised free cash flow £1.6bn (+25% vs £1.3bn); basic EPS 10.8p (+24% vs 8.7p); capital expenditure £4.9bn (flat vs £4.9bn) — same source path.

Adjusted EBITDA is stated to exclude specific adjusting items and share of results from associates/joint ventures (definition referenced to page 220, not present in this body extract); normalised free cash flow definition referenced to page 230 (not present).

No segment revenue mix (Openreach vs EE/Consumer vs Global) appears in this extract; financial statements and group performance detail are referenced from page 46/129 onwards but are absent from the filed body.

CEO narrative: FY25 revenue declined YoY, 'driven mainly by international sales and handsets'; despite this, group grew both EBITDA and normalised free cash flow via transformation savings (>£900m annualised savings, one year into a five-year programme to remove £3bn of costs) and disciplined cost control — same source path.

Dividend: Board raised FY25 dividend by 2% to 8.16 pence per share; progressive dividend policy maintained alongside re-confirmed normalised FCF targets of £2bn in FY27 and £3bn in FY30 — Chairman letter, same source path.
No share buyback or repurchase activity mentioned in this extract.

Restructuring/modernisation: UK/international B2B separation underway; non-core divestments signed (Ireland data centres; Ireland domestic enterprise/wholesale; remaining domestic Italy operations); workforce target 75,000–90,000 by end of decade; 1.2m customers migrated off legacy PSTN — same source path.

Fibre build/outlook: full fibre reaches 18m+ premises with 6.5m connected (36%); FY26 build pace to increase 20% with aim to reach up to 5m premises; target 25m premises passed by end of FY26 and 30m premises/30m retail connectivity customers by end of decade; management frames FY27 as inflection to £2bn normalised FCF — CEO letter, same source path.

Regulation: welcomed Ofcom Telecoms Access Review for long-term certainty/predictability; industry-led switch from 'CPI+' to 'pounds and pence' consumer price increases; engagement on 2024 Autumn Budget impacts — Chairman letter, same source path.

Revenue-decline framing vs FY26: management characterises FY25 revenue fall as international/handsets-driven while EBITDA/NFCF grew; Consumer broadband base returned to growth in final quarter (first time in three years); medium-term aim to grow EBITDA faster than revenue — suggesting FY25 revenue pressure may be transitional rather than structural, though no explicit FY26 revenue/FCF forecast is given in this body.
